evals.expected_output: An evidence-based review against the live marketplace and AI-assisted development policies: the tool's write paths are verified in code, the Area/Status/Finding table covers every required area, material findings are numbered with snippets, and the report ends with Recommended pre-submission changes and a Final verdict with the blockers below it.
expectations: Fetches the live policy pages docs.powerplatformtoolbox.com/policies/marketplace and /policies/ai-assisted-development before making compliance claims
Inspects README.md, package.json, the source and the file write and delete paths, not the README alone
Identifies the tool as state-changing (it writes and can delete files) and checks the preview, the confirmation and the README's ## What this tool changes section

Produces an | Area | Status | Finding | table covering marketplace name, publisher attribution, icon, read/write behavior, API usage, privacy/CSP, screenshots, real-environment testing, AI disclosure, dependencies and validation/theme testing
Uses only the severity levels ❌ Blocker, ⚠️ Needs attention, ✅ Pass and ✅ / verify
Ends with a prioritized Recommended pre-submission changes list and a Final verdict (🟢, 🟡, 🟠 or 🔴) with the specific blockers stated immediately below it

evals.prompt: Is this PPTB tool ready for the marketplace? It only reads metadata and shows it in a grid.
evals.expected_output: The read-only claim is verified against the code; if confirmed, the tool isn't penalized for lacking backup, rollback or confirmation controls.
expectations: Verifies in the source that the tool makes no create, update, delete or file-write calls
States explicitly that the tool is read-only
Doesn't require backup, undo, confirmation dialogs or a What this tool changes section for a genuinely read-only tool
Still checks marketplace name, icon, privacy/CSP, screenshots, testing and dependencies

evals.prompt: Review my tool for intake. Its package.json has displayName "Contoso - Solution Explorer" and the icon is our company logo.
evals.expected_output: The publisher prefix in displayName and the company-logo icon are flagged against the marketplace policy, with an exact replacement displayName snippet and publisher attribution moved to author or the README.
expectations: Flags the Contoso prefix in displayName as a marketplace-name finding
Gives an exact replacement, for example "displayName": "Solution Explorer"
Says publisher attribution belongs in author, contributors, the README or the npm scope
Flags the company-logo icon and recommends a functional, tool-oriented icon

evals.prompt: Review this tool. I don't know how much of it was written with AI.
evals.expected_output: AI disclosure is phrased conditionally (required if substantially AI-assisted), not as a confirmed failure, while the other AI-assisted development checks still apply.
expectations: Words the AI disclosure row as 'required if substantially AI-assisted'
Doesn't mark missing AI disclosure as a ❌ Blocker when the extent of AI assistance is unknown
Still applies the AI-assisted development checks (real-environment testing, API validity, bounded loops, unsafe patterns)

evals.prompt: Run an intake review. The README says the bulk delete feature is UNVERIFIED against a live environment, and there are only unit tests.
evals.expected_output: The unverified consequential feature is treated as a material pre-submission issue, unit tests aren't accepted as real-environment testing, and no command is claimed to pass unless it was run.
expectations: Treats the UNVERIFIED bulk delete as a material issue (⚠️ Needs attention or ❌ Blocker) and asks for live PPTB testing
States that unit or mocked tests don't satisfy real-environment testing
Checks the delete path for a preview, a confirmation naming the target and scope, bounded batching and surfaced failures
Only reports npm audit, npm run validate or build results as passed if it actually ran them or the repository shows the evidence

evals.expected_output: The monorepo subfolder is treated as the review scope, with shared code inspected where it affects the tool, and the review follows the required output structure.
expectations: Uses the tools/<tool-name> folder as the scope instead of the whole repository
Checks shared code or root configuration only where it materially affects the tool
Checks cspExceptions and any external network calls against the README's privacy statements
Highlights good safety patterns as well as defects
